body: Tested locally, it works as expected. I think this is a great start overall 🙂 Some feedback: - The Ribbon node should be renamed to Ribbon3D for consistency with the rest of the inheritance tree: Personally, I would prefer if it was named Line3D to match Line2D naming, but I understand why a different name is used. - An editor icon should be added for Ribbon, e.g. something like this (which is a recolored Line2D icon): ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6ca4eb7f-080b-4345-b1cf-7e19c0d36f6c) - The editor constantly redraws when a Ribbon node is present in the scene tree (even if it's invisible). Remember to enable **Show Update Spinner** in the Editor Settings to diagnose this. - There's a "ghost" node configuration warning displayed after creating a Ribbon node. This warning goes away after reloading the scene, and clicking it does nothing (no dialog is spawned): - There should be a node configuration warning when the material mode is set to **Custom** and no material is specified. - The ribbon isn't visible in the editor until you save and reload the scene. This might be related to the above "ghost warning" issue. - Beams are not visible in the editor until you change their Length property. - Likewise, changing a beam's **Mesh Alignment** mode from Billboard to Local can cause issues until the length is adjusted to force the mesh to redraw. ___ For future PRs: - Overbright/HDR colors can't be used in the gradient curve (they will be clamped). Perhaps something like https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/97604 is needed for Ribbon in the long run. (I assume it relies on vertex colors for the coloring, which can't be overbright in 4.x, as opposed to a texture.) - Is it planned to add a Texture property? There are properties to set the tiling mode, multiplier and UV pinning, so one could logically expect to be able to use a texture on the default materials. - The default material could have a property to fade trails and beams that are nearly perpendicular to the camera, to avoid obvious rotation: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6508dcda-83aa-4b52-b6aa-325a53c6e3f7 This is commonly done for beams that emulate volumetric light shafts, using a `dot()` product in the fragment shader. The TPS demo uses a custom shader for this currently. The value would be set as a threshold for the `dot()` product to start fading (`0.0` = no fade, `1.0` = start fading as soon as it's not perfectly perpendicular to the camera).

Needs two lines to be updated to make it work with physics interpolation enabled.

I didn't check any of the other code.

I could notice z-fighting among long living trails (e.g. in @Calinou's test project, when shooting a wall quickly in a horizontal straight line pattern).

Tested again, physics interpolation works well now.

Also, I noticed the Beam mode is gone now. Is it planned to be reimplemented later on?
I am afraid I can't quite suggest "content" to add, mostly rapid-fire style changes.

I confirm the interpolation changes I requested were integrated.

Here is a video of the z-fighting I mentioned before:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3d628c6d-ed68-45d8-b367-e02b9e42476c

You should be using CUSTOM0 instead of passing custom data in the NORMAL attribute.

To keep things simple on the implementation side, just always pass normals and tangents as usual and add the billboarding metadata in CUSTOM0. If you are concerned about bandwidth, then enable compression and write compressed vertices directly which will save a lot of bandwidth
